rics.meaning: Approved Foreign Investment — investment commitments approved by BKPM (Investment Coordinating Board). Quarterly release.
rics.how_to_use: Approval ≠ realization. BKPM also publishes 'realization' data — typically realization runs 70-90% of approvals over 1-2 year window. Surge in approvals leads BoP FDI flows by 2-4 quarters.

rics.meaning: FDI inflows from Africa — minor FDI source. Mostly South Africa-routed mining-sector investments.
rics.how_to_use: Niche bilateral. Track for niche commodity-sector flows. Most African investment flows to Indonesia run through South African mining majors with Indonesian operations.

rics.meaning: FDI inflows from Japan — long-standing major FDI source. Japanese OEMs (Toyota, Honda, Mitsubishi) and trading houses (Mitsui, Marubeni, Sumitomo) dominate.
rics.how_to_use: ~10-15% of Indonesia FDI. Concentrated in autos, manufacturing, mining. Stable bilateral relationship. Monitor for major project announcements (e.g., new auto plants, gas field developments).

rics.meaning: FDI inflows from Singapore — largest single FDI source. Often pass-through capital from ultimate owners in HK, China, US, and other jurisdictions routing through Singapore for tax/legal reasons.
rics.how_to_use: Singapore consistently #1 FDI source (~30-40% of total). Flow swings driven by major M&A deals + new investment commitments. Track for total FDI cycle direction; less reliable for ultimate-owner attribution.

rics.meaning: FDI inflows from USA — US corporate investment in Indonesia. Smaller than Singapore/Japan FDI flows.
rics.how_to_use: Concentrated in oil/gas (ExxonMobil, Chevron historically), mining (Freeport), digital (data centers, internet platforms). Recent surge in semiconductor/AI infrastructure investment. Track for geopolitical-tilt signal — Indonesia values balance between US/China FDI sources.

rics.meaning: FDI inflows from United Kingdom — UK corporate investment in Indonesia. Concentrated in oil/gas (BP), banking (HSBC, Standard Chartered), retail.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks UK-Indonesia bilateral. Brexit effects re-routing some flows. Watch for trade-deal negotiations.
